items.prompt: Which sentence is a question?
hints: A question asks something.
Questions end with a special mark.
Look for the mark that curls at the top.
items.explanation: Where is my hat? asks something, so it is a question. It ends with a question mark.

options.why: This tells us something.
This tells us something.

items.prompt: What goes at the end? 'What is your name'
hints: Read it out loud. Does it ask something?
What is an asking word.
Questions need a curly mark at the end.
items.explanation: What is your name? asks something. A question ends with a question mark.

options.why: This sentence asks something.
This is not a shout or a big feeling.

items.prompt: Is it a question or a telling sentence? Sort them.
hints: Read each one out loud.
A question asks something and wants an answer.
Start with Can you swim. Does it ask something?
items.explanation: Can you swim, Is it raining and Do you like mangoes are questions. The others tell us something.

items.prompt: Which word often starts a question?
hints: Think of words that ask.
Who, where and when are asking words too.
Which word could start: ___ is that?
items.explanation: What is a question word, like who, where and when.

options.why: The starts many telling sentences.
My starts many telling sentences.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows a big feeling?
hints: A big feeling can be surprise or joy.
Big feelings end with a special mark.
Look for the mark that is a line with a dot under it.
items.explanation: Wow, a rainbow! shows surprise. It ends with an exclamation mark.

options.why: This is a calm telling sentence.
This is a question.

items.prompt: Choose the best end mark. 'Help, my kite is stuck in the tree'
hints: Read it like the person is calling out.
Help is a word we often shout.
Shouting and strong feelings need a special mark.
items.explanation: Help! is a call out. We use an exclamation mark for shouting and strong feelings.

options.why: This does not ask a question.
A full stop is calm. This person is calling for help.

items.prompt: Choose all the questions.
hints: Three are questions.
Questions ask something.
Look at the end marks and the first words.
items.explanation: Who is at the door?, How old are you? and Can I come too? all ask something.

options.why: This tells someone to do something.
This tells us something.

items.prompt: Make it a question. Write the missing word. 'You can swim.' becomes '___ you swim?'
hints: In a question, two words swap places.
Look at the words in: You can swim.
Which word moves to the front?
items.explanation: Can moves to the front to make a question: Can you swim? It needs a capital C at the start.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.
hints: The first word has a capital letter.
The last word has a question mark.
Start with the word that has a capital letter.
items.explanation: Do you like cats? starts with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.

items.prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
hints: Check the start and the end.
Does the sentence ask something?
Find the capital letter and the question mark together.
items.explanation: Where is the cat? starts with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.

options.why: A sentence starts with a capital letter.
This asks something, so it needs a question mark.
It needs a capital letter and a question mark.

items.prompt: Which question goes with this answer? 'I am seven.'
hints: The answer is a number.
Seven tells us an age.
Which question asks about age?
items.explanation: I am seven tells your age. How old are you? asks about age.

options.why: The answer would be a name.
The answer would be a place.

items.prompt: Which one needs a question mark?
hints: Be careful. Some sentences have question words but do not ask.
A question wants someone to answer.
Which one could you answer with yes or no?
items.explanation: Can you see my ball? asks something, so it needs a question mark. I wonder where my ball is tells a thought, so it ends with a full stop.

options.text: I wonder where my ball is
options.why: This tells us what someone is thinking. It does not ask.
This tells someone to do something.
This tells someone to do something.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.
hints: A question starts with a question word.
A question ends with a question mark.
Ask where something is.
items.explanation: Where is my bag? A question ends with a question mark.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make an exclamation.
hints: The first word has a capital letter.
The last word has an exclamation mark.
It shows how big the fish is.
items.explanation: What a big fish! An exclamation ends with an exclamation mark.

items.prompt: Which sentence is a question?
hints: A question asks something.
It ends with a curly mark.
It starts with Where.
items.explanation: Where is my hat? asks something, so it ends with a question mark.

options.why: This tells us something.
This shows a strong feeling.

items.prompt: Which end mark goes here? Can you hop___
hints: The sentence asks something.
A question needs a special mark.
The mark looks like a hook with a dot.
items.explanation: Can you hop? is a question, so it needs a question mark.

options.why: A full stop is for telling sentences.
An exclamation mark shows a strong feeling.

items.prompt: Which end mark goes here? Wow, that is huge___
hints: The sentence shows a strong feeling.
Think about how you say wow.
The mark is a line with a dot below.
items.explanation: Wow, that is huge! shows a strong feeling.

options.why: It is not asking anything.
A full stop is for plain telling.

items.prompt: Which question word fits? ___ is your name?
hints: You are asking for a name.
Read the sentence aloud.
It starts with the letters Wh.
items.explanation: What is your name? asks about a thing.

options.why: When asks about time.
Where asks about a place.

items.prompt: Which question word fits? ___ do you live?
hints: You want to know a place.
Think of your house.
The word starts with Wh and ends with ere.
items.explanation: Where do you live? asks about a place.

options.why: Who asks about a person.
What asks about a thing.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences by their end mark.
hints: Questions ask something.
Telling sentences give facts.
Is it red is asking.
items.explanation: The questions need a question mark. The others tell us something.

items.prompt: Match each question to the answer.
hints: Read each question slowly.
Think about what it asks.
How old asks about age.
items.explanation: Each answer matches the question that comes before it.

items.prompt: Make it a question. Write the missing word. ___ you like milk?
hints: The sentence asks something.
It is a short word.
The word starts with D.
items.explanation: Do you like milk? is a question.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.
hints: Start with the word that has a capital letter.
The sentence ends with a question mark.
The question is about a place.

hints: The first word has a capital letter.

items.explanation: How many eggs are there? asks about a number.

items.prompt: Choose all the questions.
hints: Questions ask something.
Two of them are questions.
Look at the first word of each.
items.explanation: Is the cat sleeping? and Who made the cake? both ask something.

items.prompt: Which sentence has the right end mark?
hints: Ask yourself: is it asking?
Say it aloud with your voice going up.
A question needs a special mark.
items.explanation: Can I come too? asks something, so it ends with a question mark.
